response.sql: WITH t AS (SELECT CustomerId, SUM(Total) AS spent FROM Invoice GROUP BY CustomerId), s AS (SELECT CustomerId, spent, spent * 1.0 / (SELECT SUM(spent) FROM t) AS share FROM t), a AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT AVG(s.spent) AS avg_spent, AVG(s.share) AS avg_share, AVG(s.share - a.avg_share) AS avg_excess_over_avg_share FROM s CROSS JOIN a WHERE s.share > a.avg_share;

assumptions.assumption: The average share is taken over customers who have at least one invoice (customers with no invoices are not counted). If every customer has invoices, this is identical to counting all customers.

The 'average share' used as the cutoff is the simple mean of all customers' shares. The final 'how much their share beats the average share' is the mean of (customer share minus that overall average share) among the kept customers.
